summary: The native Android app's applicationId changes from app.switchboard.mobile to app.tn07.switchboard, the iOS bundle id, so both stores use one id. Play gets a new app record; the old record (internal track only, never published) stays unpublished. The release build reads its own Firebase client from apps/android/app/google-services.json, and the AAB verifier and mobile-release.yml accept only the new package. The Kotlin namespace, versionCode 22 / versionName 0.5.20, the debug suffix .native.dev and the upload key are unchanged. A deliberate identity change: an installed app.switchboard.mobile build is a separate app, so the user installs the new one and pairs again. No migration, because only the developer holds the internal build.

reactNativeIos.reason: The iOS bundle id is already app.tn07.switchboard (apps/mobile/app.json); only a note in apps/mobile/AGENTS.md changes, and apps/mobile/google-services.json and android.package belong to the retired Expo Android lane, left as they are.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No wire protocol or backend change. Push registration sends the Expo token, which exp.host mints for the applicationId the phone reports; the backend never reads the package.

storageDataMigration.reason: No stored data format changes. Data in the old package's sandbox is not migrated: it is a different app on Android, and the only installed copy is the developer's internal build.

automated: npm run typecheck and npm test pass.
notExercised: A signed bundleRelease AAB with the new package and its verifier run (needs the upload keystore, in CI only).
The Play upload to the new app record (the record and the publisher service account invite are manual Console steps).
A real push to a release build: EAS needs the FCM V1 service-account key assigned to app.tn07.switchboard first.
